title: Survey-start warmth had a larger high-PM than mapped-smoke slope in two eastern US bird samples in 2011-2024
abstract: We tested whether temperature has different links to two exposure indicators in a bird-survey sample. We used 10,188 accepted US runs with nearby PM2.5 in 2011-2024. Four region and period models controlled route, year, survey date, clock time and wind. The mapped medium/heavy smoke minus PM2.5-above-12 indicator slope was -10.82 and -9.07 percentage points per 5 C warmer start in East. Both four-test intervals were below zero. Western estimates were -0.62 and -0.48, with intervals across zero. State-by-year controls retained the eastern pattern, but later East results were uncertain with any smoke or a higher PM cut. These are exposure associations, not effects on birds or a causal heat effect. Total PM is not fire-only smoke. Monitor selection, daily versus dawn timing, site changes and few year clusters limit inference. The source records overlap prior campaign work. Code, aggregate results, provenance and verified input retrieval are included; external record tables remain outside the package.

display.caption: Conditional difference between mapped medium/heavy smoke and elevated total PM indicator temperature slopes. Four-test intervals use route and year clusters.
